notes: Half-life is the median age, in years, of a ruling's incoming citations from U.S. Reports opinions (citing year minus decision year; one citation per citing case). It is reported only for rulings cited at least 5 times. Data are right-censored: rulings decided recently have had little time to be cited, so their half-lives are biased low. To compare decades fairly, the by-decade chart counts only citations in each ruling's first 30 years, for rulings decided 1791 through 1984 with at least 10 such citations, and only decades with at least 30 such rulings are shown. Sudden deaths are rulings with at least 30 citations over a lifetime of 30 or more years, cited in at least 5 of the 10 years ending at the last citation, and none in the 25 or more years since. Immortals are rulings with at least 30 citations ranked by the span between first and last citing year. Only citing entries spanning at least 2 pages and at least 400 words count; short entries (orders, cert denials, under 400 words) are excluded from totals and tallied separately in orderCites, and only cited rulings spanning at least 2 pages and cited at least once are listed. Records dated before 1791 (Pennsylvania courts in volumes 1-2 Dallas) are dropped. Citations dated before the cited ruling are dropped as bad dates or mis-resolved cites. Citations come from CAP cites_to metadata, which only captures citations its parser recognized.
